mathematical_checks.topic: Full contact-preserving input and local finite discs
mathematical_checks.assessment: Block equality and Ji preservation imply ΛJi⊂Si, Bi∩ΛG0=ΛJi and Ui⊂ΩG0. Joint regular invariance excludes all regular contacts but retains contacts in ΛG0. Actual base null-coset translates shrink, their pairwise interior-disjoint Jordan discs shrink, and the matrix attractor argument gives local finiteness off ΛG0. The algebraic supplier treats the actual nonempty gap without requiring its interior.

mathematical_checks.topic: Explicit HNN tree and wall stabilizers
mathematical_checks.assessment: Independently checked edge gJ1 joins gG0 to gf^{-1}G0, well-defined via fJ1f^{-1}=J2. Immediate reversal is exactly a Britton pin. Reduced nonbacktracking closed paths are excluded by the actual algebraic supplier, and the exponent map prevents edge inversions. At a turn the translated actual gap lies inside the preceding forward disc and outside the next closed disc, giving strict nesting. This excludes repeated walls and identifies each wall stabilizer with its edge subgroup, without disc-disjointness assumptions.

mathematical_checks.topic: Regular cell neighborhoods before ambient null-wall use
mathematical_checks.assessment: A regular cell point lies on zero or one incident wall and belongs to exactly one or two vertex closed cells. Local factor disc finiteness supplies actual open one/two-cell sphere neighborhoods, with compact closure in the relevant base discontinuity sets. Any intersecting translate lies in finitely many base-group double-coordinate sets; properness of the base action leaves finitely many candidates. A fixed point preserves a vertex or an unoriented edge; no inversions and base freeness exclude a nonidentity stabilizer. Shrinking gives genuine regularity in ΩG before invoking the ambient null-coset theorem.

mathematical_checks.topic: Full ambient blocks, null walls and exact nested-limit classification
mathematical_checks.assessment: Regular seams are precisely invariant and Si∩ΛG=ΛJi, so the actual null-family supplier applies to ambient G with unchanged rank1 clearance. Distinct walls correspond to distinct cosets. Infinite nonbacktracking forward discs shrink to a point; for a new point, choosing sufficiently later walls inside earlier open discs gives pairwise disjoint nesting. Conversely the half-side toward any fixed vertex contains two fixed points of its closed cell, so sufficiently small nesting sides point away from that vertex and lie in outgoing open discs. Their nesting limit therefore avoids every old vertex limit set. The matrix attracting-limit test puts it in ΛG.

mathematical_checks.topic: Non-base element classification with enlarged cusp ranks
mathematical_checks.assessment: A cyclically reduced non-base word gives a bi-infinite tree path through pin-free powers. Null forward discs yield the two fixed endpoint limits. If the element is parabolic those coincide on an axis wall and hence in the associated subgroup limit set. The supplied full-field matrix Shimizu estimate bounds ambient orbit heights at a parabolic point, excluding its conicality in every subgroup. The actual GF criterion or the explicit elementary subgroup alternatives then makes it a subgroup parabolic point. No boundedness or rank-preservation assertion about the ambient cusp is inferred.

Q is the base regular cell and locally a sphere region with one Jordan half-disc boundary chart; full closed Jordan parametrizations justify the topological charts without smoothness. Joint regular invariance gives two disjoint labeled boundary quotients, even when original closed walls contact in the limit set. ΩG is the union of regular vertex cells. Exact one/two-cell membership leaves only base identifications and the f seam pairing; the actual local sphere patch proves the welded quotient homeomorphism and supplies holomorphic transition maps. The literal SpaceII clause(8) cut-space omission is not used.

For x∈D0 outside B1∪B2, membership in any other base translate of Bi would yield a second D0 representative via the given Ji maximality, a contradiction. Thus D0∩A=D0∩A0. Its interior representatives and its two paired seam representative sets give exactly one representative after retaining the first face and deleting the second. This proves the stated fundamental set and does not assert smooth sides or a constrained domain.

The authentic SpaceII text explicitly omits structural clauses1–8; their statements and Lemma3.2 were read, but those omissions are not suppliers. The new13-row proof supplies the missing local arguments. The separate output conical/bounded-parabolic/GF obligations and original hyperbolization/application compatibility remain unresolved outside this review.
